To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) cloud-based architectures for geoportals are needed, (2) cloud-based architectures are generic and open, and (3) cloud-based architectures can be applied in different contexts.

the presented cloud-based architectural design is a generic and open architecture for auto-scalable Web-based geoportals, which can be applied to any geoportal, and that the presented architecture is adapted to both public clouds and private clouds.

(1) the cloudification of the Swiss academic GeoVITe geoportal is feasible and (2) two generic and open architectural designs for auto-scaling Web geoportals towards the cloud are presented, which are adaptable to both public and to private cloud infrastructures.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of cloud-based architectures for Web geoportals and their implementation for the Swiss academic geoportals GeoVITe, and with the evaluation and comparison of the presented cloud-based architectures for geoportals with the current GeoVITe implementation.
the cloudification of the GeoVIte Swiss academic geoportal, a Web geoportal that offers a large number of geoportals and spatial data services to the Swiss academic community.
the development of cloud-based architectures for the cloudification of Web geoportals and the migration of a geoportal from a local to a cloud-based environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cloud-based architectures for geoportals are generic, open, and scalable and can be applied to any Web geoportal, regardless of its size, scope, or domain.
the presented cloud-based architectures for Web geoportals can be applied to any Web geoportal, and that they can serve as a reference for other academic SDIs and Web geoportales.
the cloudification of the GeoViTe Swiss academic geoportal was a success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cloudification of the geoportal GeoVite has been successful.
cloud computing has redefined how academic SDIs and Web geoportaals are designed, maintained, and operated.
the presented architectures can be used as a reference for the cloudification of Web geoportals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cloudification of a Web geoportal requires an in-depth knowledge of the cloud computing paradigm, the design of a generic architecture that considers the most important functional requirements and non-functional requirements (e.g., auto-scaling, security, performance, and reliability), and the selection of a proper cloud platform.
the cloudification of geoportals is feasible and that the presented cloud-based architectures are generic and can be used as a starting point for the cloudification of any academic geoportal.
a Web geoportal can be cloudified without the need of a complete re-engineering of its software stack.
